title: KernelConvolutionalPerceptron.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Strict separation by a bilinear convolutional model: find (c,v) in R^k × R^d such that <Σ_j c_j S^j D_i,v> > 0 for every sample. These constraints are nonconvex in the jointly trained parameters; no scalar optimization objective is specified.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query selects one of N=samples+1 samples and a parameter pair; the reply contains the exact gradient of that sample's bilinear margin with respect to both parameter blocks. Replies have no noise or history dependence.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same query returns the exact selected sample margin, alongside its gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean parameter space R^k × R^d, with d>0 and k≥2. S is the cyclic coordinate shift; k need not equal d.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/KernelConvolutionalPerceptron.lean: Filter, Space, shifted, spec.valid; LongTails/Setups/TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.lean: Features, shift.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details:
Write g=lower, R=upper, μ=contrast, κ=derivativeMargin. Hidden data admit D_i=(a_i/√2)axis+μu_i, g≤|a_i|≤R, <axis,u_i>=0, ||u_i||≤1/√k, and a common unit separator z with <z,H_k u_i>≥κ, where H_k u=(1−1/k)^(-1/2)(u−k^(-1)Σ_{j=0}^{k−1}S^j u). All scalar parameters and dimensions are public; the decomposition and separator are not supplied.
0<g≤R, 0<μ≤R, 0<κ≤1, and μ²(R/g)^4 log²(128kR²/(κμ)²)≤kκ⁶R²/10¹³. The allowed family starts at (e_0,0), cycles through all samples, and uses a fixed positive step along the returned gradient exactly when the margin is nonpositive.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence:
LongTails/Setups/KernelConvolutionalPerceptron.lean: Geometry, highPass, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.admissible.
LongTails/Setups/KernelConvolutionalPerceptron.lean: spec.valid, identityFilter, family, spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The final output must have strictly positive margin on every one of the samples. There is no epsilon tolerance or prescribed positive output margin.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Success is required for every outcome ω, rather than merely almost surely or in expectation, under a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines bilinear convolutional separation with a specific background–defect decomposition, common high-pass separator, stringent contrast regime, and prescribed cyclic update family.

descriptionHtml:
Kernel Convolutional Perceptron

We study strict separation of n+1 vectors in Rd by a kernel convolutional perceptron with parameters (c,w)∈Rk×Rd, where d≥1, k≥2, and n≥0 are integers. Each vector consists of a nonzero constant background and a small centered defect; normalized high-pass defects share a unit separator with positive margin. The parameters satisfy a quantitative small-contrast condition. The oracle returns a sample’s bilinear convolutional margin and its update direction. Starting from the identity filter and zero readout, the method cycles through samples with a fixed positive step size. The goal is strictly positive margins on every sample, for every realization.

Write the data as b0,…,bn∈Rd. Inner products and norms on each factor are Euclidean. Let S be the cyclic shift defined by (Su)ℓ=u(ℓ−1)modd for 0≤ℓ<d, and set a=d−1/2(1,…,1). For c∈Rk, b,w∈Rd, define the response and margin by Ccb=∑j=0k−1cjSjb,mi(c,w)=⟨Ccbi,w⟩. The task is to find parameters for which all these margins are strictly positive. The algorithm receives d,k,n and the scalars g,R,μ,κ specified below; the data are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Parameter regime). The integer parameters satisfy d≥1, k≥2, and n≥0. The real parameters satisfy 0<g≤R,0<μ≤R,0<κ≤1, and μ2(Rg)4[log⁡(128kR2(κμ)2)]2≤kκ6R21013.

Assumption 2 (Background and defect geometry). Define the high-pass operator on Rd by Hku=11−1/k(u−1k∑j=0k−1Sju). There exist background coefficients β0,…,βn∈R, defects u0,…,un∈Rd, and a separator v∈Rd with ∥v∥=1 such that, for every 0≤i≤n, bi=βi2a+μui,g≤|βi|≤R,⟨a,ui⟩=0,∥ui∥≤1k,⟨v,Hkui⟩≥κ.

At a query (i,(c,w))∈{0,…,n}×(Rk×Rd), the oracle returns exactly (mi(c,w),Gi(c,w)), where Gi(c,w)=((⟨Sjbi,w⟩)j=0k−1,Ccbi).

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze the kernel convolutional perceptron with cyclic sample selection and simultaneous updates of the filter and readout. The algorithm chooses a fixed step size η>0 from its inputs and initializes θ0=(c0,w0)=(e0,0),i0=0, where e0=(1,0,…,0)∈Rk. At each iteration it queries (it,θt) and applies θt+1={θt+ηGit(θt),mit(θt)≤0,θt,mit(θt)>0,it+1=(it+1)mod(n+1). The sample cursor advances after every query, including queries that leave the parameters unchanged. After T oracle calls, the output is the current pair θ¯=(c¯,w¯)=θT. Its required accuracy is exact strict separation: mi(c¯,w¯)>0for every i∈{0,…,n}, for every realization of any algorithmic randomness.

The oracle gives one exact sample margin and gradient. The setup requires cyclic QPA, identity filter and zero readout initialization, positive constant step, and updates only at nonpositive margins. Kernel convolutional perceptron: KernelConvolutionalPerceptron.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) KernelConvolutionalPerceptronAcceleration (Ours) (review) O(N(R/g)2κ−3log⁡kRκμ); η=κ/(16k/2R).
(2) Fixed high-pass perceptron, derived bound (Kernel-Size-k Convolutional QPA on Many-Sample Data, n.d.) O(N(1+(kκ2)−1)), same sample oracle; readout-only updates. (1): No established improvement in separation complexity. (1) costs more throughout its admissible regime; (2) has no contrast dependence or small-contrast restriction.
(3) Data recovery and offline LP, derived bound (Kernel-Size-k Convolutional QPA on Many-Sample Data, n.d.) O(N) sample calls; offline computation excluded. (1): No established improvement in oracle complexity. (1) pays the extra factor (R/g)2κ−3log⁡(kR/(κμ)).
(4) Clustered QPA (LongTails, n.d.) O(N(R/g)2[1+log⁡(R/μ)]); k=2, ∥ui−u⋆∥≤κ/64. (1): Removes the residual cap and κ-dependent initialization; covers arbitrary kernel sizes and unaligned, negatively correlated, growing-rank residuals. (1): Worse κ−3 dependence and leading constant on the overlap; stricter contrast condition; step still needs κ.
(5) Noisy QPA (Tyurin 2026, Theorem 5.1) O(dνA[1+log⁡(dA/ν)]); probability 1−ρ; k=N=2, dataset (5), 0<ν≤1/10. (1): Method-specific guarantee for k>2, arbitrary N, identity start without noise, deterministic separation. Classes are incomparable; no rate comparison. (1) excludes (5)’s pure-reference sample (κ=0); requires positive residual margin for every sample.

Abbr: e=d−1/21; P is the cyclic shift; Hk=(1−1/k)−1/2(I−k−1∑j<kPj); QPA: quadratic perceptron algorithm; LP: linear program. In (5), ν is the unnormalized defect amplitude, ρ∈(0,1), q=∥θ0∥2/|⟨θ0,vν,+⟩|2<∞, vν,+ is the positive defect eigenvector, and A=(1+log⁡(q/ρ3))(1+log⁡(dq/ν)); the step and injected noise are tuned as in Theorem 5.1.

source:
import LongTails.Setups.ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron

open OracleTemplate
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.KernelConvolutionalPerceptron

abbrev Features := TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.Features
abbrev Filter (k : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)
abbrev Space (k d : ℕ) := Filter k × Features d
noncomputable abbrev axis := ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron.axis
abbrev Data (d n : ℕ) := Fin (n + 1) → Features d
abbrev Query (k d n : ℕ) := Fin (n + 1) × Space k d

noncomputable def shifted {d : ℕ} (j : ℕ) (b : Features d) : Features d :=
  (TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.shift)^[j] b

noncomputable def response {k d : ℕ} (c : Filter k) (b : Features d) : Features d :=
  ∑ j : Fin k, c j • shifted j b

noncomputable def margin {k d : ℕ} (b : Features d) (θ : Space k d) : ℝ :=
  ⟪response θ.1 b, θ.2⟫

noncomputable def direction {k d : ℕ} (b : Features d) (θ : Space k d) : Space k d :=
  (WithLp.toLp 2 fun j => ⟪shifted j b, θ.2⟫, response θ.1 b)

noncomputable def highPass (k : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (u : Features d) : Features d :=
  (Real.sqrt (1 - (k : ℝ)⁻¹))⁻¹ • (u - (k : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ j : Fin k, shifted j u)

structure Geometry {d n : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (D : Data d n) (g R μ κ : ℝ) where
  background : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ
  defect : Fin (n + 1) → Features d
  separator : Features d
  sample_eq : ∀ i, D i = (background i / Real.sqrt 2) • axis d + μ • defect i
  background_lower : ∀ i, g ≤ |background i|
  background_upper : ∀ i, |background i| ≤ R
  centered : ∀ i, ⟪axis d, defect i⟫ = 0
  defect_norm : ∀ i, ‖defect i‖ ≤ (Real.sqrt k)⁻¹
  separator_unit : ‖separator‖ = 1
  derivative_margin : ∀ i, κ ≤ ⟪separator, highPass k (defect i)⟫

structure Reply (k d : ℕ) where
  margin : ℝ
  direction : Space k d

noncomputable def answer {k d n : ℕ} (D : Data d n) (query : Query k d n) : Reply k d :=
  ⟨margin (D query.1) query.2, direction (D query.1) query.2⟩

def Separates {k d n : ℕ} (D : Data d n) (θ : Space k d) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < margin (D i) θ

noncomputable def identityFilter (k d : ℕ) : Space k d :=
  (WithLp.toLp 2 fun j => if j.val = 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0, 0)

def family {k d n : ℕ} (A : Algorithm (Query k d n) (Reply k d) (Space k d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (point : A.State → Space k d) (cursor : A.State → Fin (n + 1)) (η : ℝ),
    0 < η ∧
    (∀ seed, point (A.initial seed) = identityFilter k d ∧ cursor (A.initial seed) = 0) ∧
    (∀ s, A.query s = (0, (cursor s, point s))) ∧
    (∀ s r, point (A.update s r) =
      if r.margin ≤ 0 then point s + η • r.direction else point s) ∧
    (∀ s r, cursor (A.update s r) = finRotate (n + 1) (cursor s)) ∧
    (∀ s, A.output s = point s)

structure Params where
  dimension : ℕ
  kernel : ℕ
  samples : ℕ
  lower : ℝ
  upper : ℝ
  contrast : ℝ
  derivativeMargin : ℝ

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Data p.dimension p.samples
  Query p := Query p.kernel p.dimension p.samples
  Reply p := Reply p.kernel p.dimension
  Output p := Space p.kernel p.dimension
  publicInput := id
  valid p :=
    0 < p.dimension ∧ 2 ≤ p.kernel ∧ 0 < p.lower ∧ p.lower ≤ p.upper ∧ 0 < p.contrast ∧
      p.contrast ≤ p.upper ∧ 0 < p.derivativeMargin ∧ p.derivativeMargin ≤ 1 ∧
      p.contrast ^ 2 * (p.upper / p.lower) ^ 4 *
        Real.log (128 * p.kernel * p.upper ^ 2 / (p.derivativeMargin * p.contrast) ^ 2) ^ 2 ≤
        p.kernel * p.derivativeMargin ^ 6 * p.upper ^ 2 / 10 ^ 13
  admissible p D oracle :=
    Nonempty (Geometry p.kernel D p.lower p.upper p.contrast p.derivativeMargin) ∧
    ∀ history query seed, oracle.answer history query seed = answer D query.2
  successful _ D output _ := ∀ ω, Separates D (output ω)
  allowedAlgorithm _ := family

end LongTails.Setups.KernelConvolutionalPerceptron
